ing: finely minced; or use clams or shrimp
minced, such as goat pepper or habanero
st: Mince the conch very fine, almost to a paste, or pulse it in a food processor.
Whisk [[1 cup]] flour, [[1 tsp]] baking powder, [[1 tsp]] salt and the black pepper in a bowl.
Beat in the egg and [[0.5 cup]] milk until a thick batter forms.
Fold in the conch, bell pepper, onion, celery, chili and the juice of [[1 lime]].
Rest the batter for 10 minutes.
Heat [[3 cups]] oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Drop tablespoon-size scoops into the oil, 5 or 6 at a time. Fry 3 to 4 minutes, turning once, until deep golden.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with lime wedges or a mayonnaise dip.
Place each conch steak between plastic wrap and pound with a mallet until about 1/4 inch thick and tender.
Rub the conch with the juice of [[1 lime]], [[0.5 tsp]] salt and the black pepper.
Mix [[1 cup]] flour, [[1 tsp]] salt and the garlic powder on a plate.
Whisk the eggs with [[0.25 cup]] milk in a shallow dish.
Dip each steak in the egg mix, then coat in seasoned flour. Rest on a rack for 5 minutes.
Heat [[2 cups]] oil in a deep skillet to 350°F (175°C).
Fry 2 or 3 pieces at a time for 1 to 2 minutes per side until golden. Do not overcook or the conch turns tough.
Drain on paper towels and serve with lime wedges.

ing: diced small; or use fresh raw shrimp or scallops
st: Rinse the conch and dice it into pieces about 1/4 inch wide. Use only very fresh conch kept cold.
Place it in a glass bowl and cover with the juice of [[4 limes]] and [[1 orange]].
Cover and refrigerate 30 minutes, stirring once, until the conch turns opaque and firm.
Dice the tomatoes, onion, bell pepper and celery.
Mince the hot pepper, wearing gloves, and keep the seeds out for less heat.
Add the vegetables, hot pepper and [[0.5 tsp]] salt to the conch and toss.
Chill 10 more minutes, taste, and add lime or salt as needed. Serve cold.

ing: 15 oz, drained; or fresh or frozen
st: Rinse [[2 cups]] rice in cold water and drain well.
Cook the bacon in a heavy pot with [[1 tbsp]] oil over medium heat for 5 minutes until crisp.
Add the onion, bell pepper and celery and cook 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in [[2 tbsp]] tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes until it darkens.
Add the pigeon peas, thyme, [[4 cups]] water, [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper. Bring to a boil.
Stir in the rice, cover, and cook on the lowest heat for 20 minutes.
Remove from the heat, rest 10 minutes covered, remove the thyme stems, and fluff.

ing: cold, plus more for the pan
st: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C) and grease an 8-inch round pan with butter.
Mix [[3 cups]] flour, [[1 tbsp]] baking powder, [[3 tbsp]] sugar and [[0.5 tsp]] salt in a bowl.
Rub in [[4 tbsp]] cold butter with your fingertips until it looks like coarse crumbs.
Pour in [[1 cup]] milk and stir until the dough just comes together. Do not overmix.
Knead the dough gently 5 or 6 times on a floured counter.
Pat the dough into the pan about 1 inch thick.
Bake 30 minutes until golden brown on top and a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool 10 minutes, then cut into wedges and serve with butter or stewed fish.

ing: or grouper, cut into large pieces
st: Rub the fish with the juice of [[2 limes]], [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper and let it sit for 10 minutes.
Pat dry and dust lightly with [[1 tbsp]] flour.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a wide pan and brown the fish for 2 minutes per side. Lift it out.
Add [[1 tbsp]] oil and [[2 tbsp]] flour to the pan and stir for 2 minutes until golden brown, making a roux.
Add the onion, celery and garlic and cook 5 minutes.
Stir in the tomatoes, thyme, whole hot pepper and [[1.5 cups]] water. Simmer 10 minutes until thickened into a gravy.
Return the fish and spoon the gravy over it. Cover and cook 8 minutes until the fish flakes.
Season with [[0.5 tsp]] salt, remove the hot pepper, and serve with grits or rice.

ing: ripe or canned, peeled and chopped; or guava paste
optional; or use 1 tsp vanilla instead
st: Mix [[3 cups]] flour, [[1 tbsp]] baking powder, [[0.5 cup]] sugar and [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Rub in [[3 tbsp]] butter, then stir in the egg and [[0.75 cup]] milk to form a soft dough.
Roll the dough on a floured counter into a rectangle about 10 by 14 inches.
Spread [[2 cups]] chopped guava across the dough, leaving a 1-inch border, and roll up like a jelly roll. Pinch the ends.
Wrap in greased foil, leaving room to expand.
Set on a rack in a pot with 2 inches of boiling water. Cover and steam for 1.5 hours, adding more hot water as needed.
For the sauce, beat [[3 tbsp]] butter, [[1.5 cups]] powdered sugar, [[0.25 cup]] evaporated milk and optional [[2 tbsp]] rum until smooth. Heat gently.
Slice the duff and pour the warm sauce over each piece.
